approachQuestion.prompt:
Remove contained ranges

Given closed intervals [start,end] where start≤end, return only intervals that are not contained in any other input interval. Return survivors ordered by start ascending then end ascending. First collapse exact duplicate intervals to one copy, retaining the earliest input occurrence. Then remove every interval contained in another distinct interval. 1≤n≤200000; integer endpoints within ±10^9. Examples: [[1,5],[2,3],[1,5],[6,7]]→[[1,5],[6,7]]; [[2,4],[1,5]]→[[1,5]]. Do not modify either input. Values are opaque comparison keys; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside the stated model. Choose the most efficient valid method.
constraints: Inputs are read-only and must remain unchanged.
Only comparison-based ordering is allowed; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside this problem model.

options.text: Sort indexed intervals by start ascending, end descending, then original index; scan while tracking the furthest end, retaining only noncontained ranges and earliest exact duplicate.
options.feedback: An enclosing range with equal start comes first; the prefix maximum detects containment and index resolves exact duplicates.

options.text: Sort by start and end ascending; discard a range only if its immediate predecessor contains it.
options.feedback: A contained interval can appear after several unrelated ranges; checking only the immediate predecessor misses the maximum earlier end. For [[1,10],[2,3],[4,5]], [4,5] is contained by [1,10] although its immediate predecessor [2,3] does not contain it.

options.text: Compare every range against every other range; remove contained copies except the earliest duplicate.
options.feedback: Correct, but pairwise comparison is avoidable.

options.text: Sort by start descending and retain ranges whose end exceeds all previously seen ends.
options.feedback: The direction is reversed; for [[1,5],[2,3]] this keeps the contained range.

feedback.reason: Equal starts put the widest interval first, so a later smaller end is known contained.
details: Sort indexed ranges by start ascending, end descending, then original index. For each exact interval retain only its earliest indexed occurrence. Scan the resulting order while tracking the greatest end; discard a range if its end is no greater than that maximum, since a distinct earlier range contains it.

Equal starts put the widest interval first, so a later smaller end is known contained. Deduplicate exact intervals using earliest original index before the maximum-end test; identical copies otherwise obscure the distinct-interval rule.

“Sort indexed intervals by start ascending, end descending, then original index; scan while tracking the furthest end, retaining only noncontained ranges and earliest exact duplicate.”: An enclosing range with equal start comes first; the prefix maximum detects containment and index resolves exact duplicates.

“Sort by start and end ascending; discard a range only if its immediate predecessor contains it.”: A contained interval can appear after several unrelated ranges; checking only the immediate predecessor misses the maximum earlier end. For [[1,10],[2,3],[4,5]], [4,5] is contained by [1,10] although its immediate predecessor [2,3] does not contain it.
“Compare every range against every other range; remove contained copies except the earliest duplicate.”: Correct, but pairwise comparison is avoidable.
“Sort by start descending and retain ranges whose end exceeds all previously seen ends.”: The direction is reversed; for [[1,5],[2,3]] this keeps the contained range.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed below, choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space bounds. Count working copies, event/heap/visited storage and sort buffers; exclude the caller input and returned output. Comparisons and arithmetic take constant time; merge sort uses a linear buffer.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Sort indexed ranges and track the greatest previously retained end.
details: Sorting n indexed intervals costs O(n log n), with comparator tie fields evaluated in constant work. Equal-range grouping and the maximum-end scan each consume all records once. The indexed copy and merge buffer occupy O(n) space; no containment test scans every earlier interval separately.
